clue.text: Point to publication's incitement to riot

parts.note: S is south, one of the compass points
an edition is one printing or issue of a publication; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a newspaper's inflammatory piece as stirring up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point here, S for south, not a verb meaning indicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or conduct that stirs people to rebel against authority, which is incitement to riot.

explanation.surface: Someone marches stiffly and says the corset stays are responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Struts are proud, stiff steps, and struts are also braces or supports in a framework, which are stays.

explanation.surface: A fair penalty is imposed for wasting things.
explanation.definitionFit: One's desert is what one deserves, a fitting punishment, and a desert is a barren wasteland.

clue.text: Bore about a daughter's dressing down

indicators.note: about means the word for bore surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to tire someone is to bore them
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A tiresome man grumbles over how his daughter is dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing down' looks like clothing but means a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism, which is what a dressing down is.

clue.text: Her view got misrepresented — a personal problem

definitions.note: the adjective serves as a noun here: being too heavy is a personal problem

indicators.note: misrepresented means the words her view got are presented in a wrong order

explanation.surface: She feels her opinion was twisted on something private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her view got' are the letters; 'misrepresented' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying excess body weight is a common private worry, a problem a person has with themselves.

indicators.note: involving means the word for row wraps around the doctor's letters

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A board meeting turns into a quarrel with the doctor at the centre of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel (rhymes with cow) but is a line of seats, a TIER. MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a common crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Board as a noun is a plank of sawn wood, and sawn wood generally is called timber.

clue.text: Line on map is nothing to the fighting men

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing
taken as written
RM, the Royal Marines, are fighting men

explanation.surface: A position on a map is of no value to the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is the Royal Marines, the British navy's soldiers. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line drawn on a weather map joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: Sort of teasing only adolescents find agreeable?

definitions.text: Sort of teasing only adolescents find agreeable?

parts.words: Sort of teasing only adolescents find agreeable?
parts.note: split into three words, the word means unpleasant at a certain stage of life, so it is playful banter that suits only those whose age is bad

explanation.surface: A kind of mockery that only teenagers enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is to split the word as BAD IN AGE: teenagers, at an awkward age, would like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful banter, a sort of teasing.

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: in means the letter for quiet goes inside the word for schools

parts.note: sects are schools of thought
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Testimonials about keeping silence in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' means schools of thought, SECTS, not places of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sense of points or details referred to, as in 'in some respects', respects are matters of reference.

explanation.surface: Something was held back from a person who was about to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means kept back for later use, and it also describes a shy, quiet, retiring nature.

indicators.note: Sound tells the solver to swap a word for another that is pronounced the same

parts.note: hoards are stores, stockpiles put away

explanation.surface: Shops with good sound systems attract the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid or good, but it signals a word pronounced like HOARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large, unruly masses of people, a synonym for crowds.

clue.text: Refuse to mark the page of one's book

definitions.text: mark the page of one's book

explanation.surface: A reader declines to dog-ear the pages of their book.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to refuse it, and turning down a page corner folds it over to mark a place.

explanation.surface: Money, it is said, makes all the difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is loose coins or cash, and a change is any alteration, something that makes things different.

clue.text: Washes not before time -for a fresh start

parts.note: cleans means washes
late means not before the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone finally washes up, overdue, to make a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean slate is a record wiped clear, so a new beginning with past faults forgotten.

clue.text: The man responsible for the grind!

definitions.text: The man responsible for the grind!

parts.words: The man responsible for the grind!
parts.note: the grind sounds like a hard daily slog, but read literally it is the grinding of corn, so the man responsible builds and runs the machinery that grinds

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for the daily drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the grind' suggests tedious hard work; taken literally it is the grinding of grain in a mill, the trade of the person who builds and maintains mill machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A millwright designs, builds and repairs the machinery of mills, which grind corn.

indicators.note: freely means the letters of broad lea are used without fixed order

explanation.surface: A lovely wide meadow is open for anyone to use.
explanation.walkthrough: A lea is a meadow; 'freely' signals the rearrangement and 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming and lovable, very delightful.

parts.note: in means favoured or fashionable, as in the in crowd
spirit is distilled strong drink such as whisky

explanation.surface: A preferred stiff drink to perk someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit someone is to fill them with spirit and energy, so to enliven them.

indicators.note: making here means the letters of defer tea are made into something new

explanation.surface: Perhaps postpone making the tea before meeting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-making' reads as brewing tea, but 'making' is the anagram signal on DEFER TEA. 'Maybe' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to join into a union or league, a political form of getting together.

clue.text: Press the German leader to find the dope

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
der is a German word for the
a head is a leader, as of a school or department

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a German boss to track down a drug supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but is a fool. DUN means to press for payment of a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and a dunderhead is a slow-witted blockhead.

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Spite displayed by a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, the spirit behind vindictive acts.

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A country house in England passed down the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like an adjective describing the inheritance; it is the noun STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is all the property they leave, which passes to heirs as an inheritance.

clue.text: Little creature of nicest possible disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so a possible disposition of the letters of nicest is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tiny animal with the sweetest temperament imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament but means arrangement; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are small six-legged animals, a typical little creature.

clue.text: A weapon presented for repair, being faulty

indicators.note: being faulty suggests the item is broken, signalling that the letters of repair are muddled

explanation.surface: A sword is handed in to be mended because it is defective.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'being faulty' sits after 'repair', which looks like the reason for handing the weapon in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword, a kind of weapon.

indicators.note: the end says the short word in goes at the finish of the answer

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden, and the plural asks for two of them
the second of the two beasts, another ass

explanation.surface: Some criminal creatures meet their end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beasts' gives two asses, side by side; 'in the end' puts IN after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired or political killer, one kind of criminal.

explanation.surface: A plain phrase for desks and cabinets bought for a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a government department or agency, and also a writing desk with drawers, a piece of furniture.

parts.note: the clue reads like someone braced to get drenched in rain, but describes a liquid mixture made ready to steep food in before cooking

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves for getting drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' suggests a person ready to get wet; here it is a cook's preparation, a liquid that meat or fish is soaked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid prepared so that food can steep in it to gain flavour.

parts.note: admission to a course sounds like enrolling in a class or entering a racecourse, but the course is part of a meal and the word also means right of entry

explanation.surface: Someone asks about getting into a racecourse or a class.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the right of entry somewhere and a dish served as a course of a meal; 'course' suggests a racecourse or class.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is the right of admission to a place or circle, and also a dish served as a course at dinner.

clue.text: Opinion held about people getting a flat

indicators.note: held about means the word for opinion is wrapped around the word for people

parts.note: a tenet is a held opinion or principle
men are people, as in the men of a team

explanation.surface: A view is shared among people about getting an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a set of rooms rented as a dwelling, in Scotland an apartment block, so a flat.
